title: Stratification in Southeast Asia’s semiconductor supply chain: Evidence from the perspective of intra-industry trade
summary: Amidst the profound geo-economic restructuring of the global semiconductor supply chain, this study quantifies the Grubel-Lloyd (GL) index to measure the extent of intra-industry trade (IIT) for semiconductor products across six ASEAN economies during the 2021–2025 period. By employing the Grubel-Lloyd (GL) index on highly disaggregated trade data (6-digit HS codes) computed against the world, Research indicate that integration into the intra-regional production network is heterogeneous, forming a distinct multi-tiered differentiated structure. Quantitative results categorize the region into three distinct tiers: (1) High IIT (GL > 0.8) in Thailand and Vietnam, characterized by export-oriented downstream processing where high indices largely reflect processing and packaging operations conducted by foreign affiliates, albeit with positive signals of functional upgrading in supporting components; (2) Medium but mature IIT (GL = 0.616–0.836) in Singapore and Malaysia, where Singapore’s robust trade surpluses underscore its upstream dominance as a design and net component supplier, while Malaysia solidifies its midstream integration by transitioning toward advanced Assembly, Testing, and Packaging (ATP); and (3) low and volatile IIT (GL = 0.557 on the period mean) in Indonesia, reflecting an asymmetric dependence on imported inputs. The Philippines is a distinct case: Its level remains high at 0.810, but it records the steepest decline in the sample, from 0.957 in 2021 to 0.686 in 2025, indicating a progressive shift toward one-way import dependence. Based on these findings, the study argues that advancing from VIIT to Horizontal Intra-Industry Trade (HIIT) is imperative. And alongside upgrading their domestic supporting industries, human capital, and infrastructure, ASEAN countries need to forge a regional production network predicated on complementary advantages. This integration is the key for the ASEAN bloc to build a self-reliant ecosystem, enhance resilience, and ascend to higher value echelons in the global technology landscape.

title: Content associations with answer selection and engagement in supply chain community question answering
summary: Community question-answering (cQA) platforms are important ecosystems for knowledge sharing, yet research on what makes an answer “best” or a question engaging has often focused on either individual lexical features or broad topics. This exploratory study examines both levels in Yahoo! Chiebukuro, asking which nouns and semantic noun clusters are associated with best-answer selection and question engagement. We analyze a large corpus of questions and answer-tier posts collected under the keyword “logistics,” using an offline machine-translation pipeline with manually validated noun-level fidelity. Best-answer selection is modeled with conditional logistic regression within question threads, controlling for answer length, order, and question-answer noun overlap. Engagement is modeled in two stages: whether a question receives any response and, conditional on receiving one, how many responses it attracts. Operational logistics nouns such as “distribution,” “warehouse,” and “center” are associated with best-answer selection, whereas broader civic and infrastructure nouns such as “car,” “tax,” and “shinkansen” are associated with higher engagement. At the cluster level, most semantic noun clusters are associated with best-answer selection, while the clusters associated with response likelihood and response volume are largely distinct. These findings reveal differentiated content-outcome profiles across answer and question levels and provide a domain-wide descriptive map of engagement and answer selection in logistics-related cQA discourse.

title: PURPOSE-DRIVEN LEADERSHIP, ESG AND EMPLOYEE ENGAGEMENT: BUILDING SUSTAINABLE BRANDS IN UZBEKISTAN
summary: This article examines the relationship between purpose-driven leadership, environmental, social and governance (ESG) practices, employee engagement, and sustainable brand development in Uzbekistan. As businesses increasingly face expectations concerning corporate responsibility, transparency, and long-term value creation, sustainability must be integrated into organizational leadership, human resource management, and brand strategy. The study adopts an integrative conceptual literature review, drawing on recent research on sustainability leadership, ESG and employee engagement, green human resource management, and corporate social responsibility in Uzbekistan. It proposes a conceptual framework in which purpose-driven leadership shapes organizational values and priorities, ESG practices translate these priorities into measurable organizational commitments, and employee engagement supports the implementation and communication of sustainability-related values. These processes may contribute to stakeholder trust and sustainable brand development when corporate commitments are supported by verifiable practices. The article also identifies contextual challenges, including limited sustainability-reporting capabilities, inconsistent implementation of ESG principles, and the risk of greenwashing. The findings provide a theoretical basis for future empirical research and practical recommendations for organizations seeking to develop credible and competitive sustainable brands in Uzbekistan.

title: Blockchain-enabled strategic pathways for enhancing offshore wind energy supply chain resilience: An integrated decision-support framework
summary: Offshore wind energy projects face disruptions due to their complexity and reliance on the global supply chain (SC), making SC resilience vital for the reliable and sustainable development of offshore wind energy. Blockchain could enhance resilience through transparency, asset tracking and information security. To strengthen the resilience of offshore wind energy SCs, this study aims to apply an integrated decision-support framework for identifying and prioritizing strategic blockchain-enabled pathways. Drawing on a review of the literature on offshore wind energy SCs, resilience and blockchain applications, the criteria are specified. Then SWOT analysis is used to formulate blockchain-based strategies. The Fuzzy Stepwise Weight Assessment Ratio Analysis (F-SWARA) and Fuzzy Measurement Alternatives and Ranking according to the COmpromise Solution (F-MARCOS) technique were used to rank the suggested strategies. To assess robustness, sensitivity analyses were conducted on criteria weights and expert weights and a comparison was performed using fuzzy decision-making techniques. Economic value and reduction of disruption costs, implementation and maintenance cost and traceability and visibility of equipment and data were the most important sub-criteria. Also, the strategies of developing a blockchain-based intelligent decision-making platform to increase SC resilience in disruption conditions, establishing a blockchain-based risk management and early warning system for SC disruptions and implementing a blockchain-based equipment tracking system were identified as the most significant proposed strategies, respectively. These findings provide context-specific insights that may inform offshore wind developers, policymakers, and SC stakeholders when considering blockchain investments and resilience-enhancing initiatives under resource and infrastructure constraints. • Introducing a strategic framework for offshore wind supply chain resilience. • Developing blockchain strategies in offshore wind projects using SWOT analysis. • Applying Fuzzy SWARA-MARCOS methods for evaluating identified strategies. • Robustness assessment using sensitivity analysis and comparison with MCDM methods. • Offering policy and managerial insights for resilient offshore wind supply chains.

title: Transforming green innovation into entrepreneurship for a sustainable future: barriers, motivators and the impact of university support systems
summary: Abstract Drawing on growing concerns about green entrepreneurship and universities’ third mission to address sustainability-related issues, this study examines the barriers and motivators perceived by university students in transforming green innovation ideas into entrepreneurial practices, as well as the impact of university support systems on the transformation. The descriptive research findings from a sample of 263 students from Finland, Albania, and Kosovo reveal that, despite having more educational and economic advantages with increasing efforts made, entrepreneurship-minded Finnish students still face a lack of knowledge, skills, and funding access at a high level, similar to those of the other two countries with less advantaged backgrounds. Besides, personal interest in environmental sustainability, as well as financial benefits and career opportunities, are perceived across the countries as key motivators in fostering intentions. Moreover, the study points out that the support mechanisms that students need most in the transformation, regardless of their backgrounds, are financing, courses, and mentorship focused on green innovation and entrepreneurship. The study makes a novel contribution by connecting universities’ third mission with green innovation and entrepreneurship through university support systems. This insight, therefore, provides universities, in collaboration with other stakeholders, with a valuable overview to develop support strategies that better prepare entrepreneurship-minded students for green entrepreneurial implementation and contribute to sustainable regional development.

title: A study analyzing factors retarding digital transformation and configuration pathways: Based on the perspective of digital transformation acceptors
summary: The high-touch service nature of the hospitality industry highlights that the success of digital transformation depends primarily on human factors rather than technology itself. Existing research indicates that approximately 80% of strategic initiatives fail due to employee resistance to change or capability deficits. Furthermore, nearly three-quarters of middle managers and staff exhibit resistance toward such transformations. This alarming trend raises a fundamental question: how can the hospitality industry navigate the inherent tension between high-touch emotional labor and digital depersonalization to transform employee resistance into proactive adoption? While traditional research frequently focuses on hotel management as change promoters, this study shifts the analytical focus to hotel employees as change recipients. Guided by cognitive appraisal and social information processing theories, within the context of hotel service scenarios, this research constructs models of resistance mitigation and antecedent condition linkages across individual, organizational, and managerial levels. Through an empirical analysis of 545 survey responses from various hotel categories and the application of fuzzy set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA), this study systematically explores the mechanisms of resistance alleviation and the synergistic effects of the identified influencing factors. Regression results indicate that digital literacy, digital strategy consensus, and perceptions of digital technology warmth and capability are negatively associated with hotel employee resistance to digital transformation. Additionally, organizational strategic flexibility and digital leadership positively moderate the relationships between these individual factors and resistance. The fsQCA results further identify two primary equifinal patterns sufficient for fostering a state of low resistance, demonstrating how strong digital leadership serves as a social cue that effectively compensates for the absence of organizational strategic flexibility. Ultimately, this research deepens the understanding of human-centered digital transformation in the hospitality sector and offers theoretical frameworks for managers to mitigate employee resistance to digital initiatives, thereby facilitating successful strategic implementation.

title: Will Systematic Stewardship Save the Planet?
summary: The largest institutional investors have solidified their status as “universal owners,” holding almost eighty percent of the U.S. stock market. The growing influence of these investors over the companies they invest in has sparked optimism among scholars and activists that asset managers will use their clout to steer firms towards Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) objectives. But such optimism ma be misplaced. Focusing on carbon emission reduction, we argue that universal owners lack the necessary incentives and competence to pressure corporations to lower emissions.Universal owners market ESG investments with conflicting promises of “doing well while doing good.” The untenable promise that ESG investments will “do well,” or match the returns of non-ESG funds, prevents universal owners from effectively “doing good,” or meaningfully compelling corporations to reduce emissions. Furthermore, although climate change is a systematic risk, addressing it requires firm-specific engagement. Universal owners, however, lack the incentive to lead firm-specific campaigns. We further demonstrate that no other actors will emerge to provide the required firm-specific engagement. We argue that universal owners’ distorted incentives should concern even those who believe that climate stewardship is necessary, albeit imperfect, in light of government inaction. We explain why extensive disclosure requirement for ESG funds would not eliminate the distortions caused by their contradictory commitments and consider implications for the ESG movement. While universal owners are ill-equipped to direct corporations toward efficient climate solutions, these investors may nudge environmental legislation forward by ensuring that their portfolio companies’ lobbying efforts are aligned with their pledges to protect the environment.

title: Strengthening of environmental justice, green dynamic capabilities, and enterprises’ green technological innovation
summary: This study examines how strengthened environmental adjudication affects corporate green technological innovation, drawing on data from Chinese A-share listed companies from 2013-2023 and the institutional context of specialised environmental judicial reform. We investigate the mediating role of green dynamic capabilities and the moderating effect of ESG performance. Judicial intervention offsets administrative deficiencies and provides stable institutional expectations, while strengthened environmental adjudication is positively associated with green innovation by enhancing firms’ green dynamic capabilities. Strong ESG performance enhances firms’ strategic responsiveness to external judicial pressures. Further analysis reveals that these effects are more pronounced in state-owned enterprises, firms in economically developed regions, and high-pollution industries. This research provides new theoretical insights into firms’ differentiated responses to environmental regulations, along with empirical evidence and policy implications for optimising environmental justice policies and targeted governance to stimulate innovation across market entities.

title: Dynamic Monitoring and Emergency Collaborative Decision-Making for Logistics Supply Chain Risks Integrating GD-AHP and MADRL
summary: Since there are various uncertain influences that affect the operation of the logistics supply chain, the existing supervision method cannot offer timely and efficient historical data, while the supply-demand relationship still needs enhancement. Therefore, this study puts forward a logistics supply chain risk dynamic monitoring and emergency collaborative decision-making framework based on Group Decision-Analytic Hierarchy Process and Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning. The framework aims to solve problems such as weak coordination in dynamic evolution and emergency decision-making of modern logistics supply chains, as well as insufficient coupling of multi-source risks. The framework first conducts risk level quantification and real-time monitoring. It combines Temporal Convolutional Network to extract spatiotemporal features and dynamically evaluate supply chain risks. It also introduces Exponentially Weighted Moving Average and other methods to generate emergency collaborative decision-making outputs. According to experimental results, the proposed model can monitor the disruption events accurately with 94.02% and the recall rate with 95.64%. In addition, the early warning delay is only 37.23 ms for monitoring the supply chain disruptions dataset under risk dynamic monitoring. In emergency coordination, the collaborative decision-making reward reaches 1.38 ± 0.10, the disruption loss reduction rate reaches 28.61% ± 8.11%, the resource utilization rate reaches 78.56%, and the task completion rate reaches 91.49%. The results clearly demonstrate that the model is superior to other models in terms of risk recognition accuracy, emergency response delay, resource use efficiency, and decision-making rewards for collaboration. The model is highly efficient in dynamic monitoring and provides effective emergency decision-making support for logistics chains. By improving risk perception, response coordination, and resource allocation efficiency, the proposed framework enhances operational resilience and disruption response capability of logistics chains.

title: Green Bonds and Financial Performance of Commercial Banks in Kenya
summary: The study investigated the relationship between green bonds and the financial performance of commercial banks in Kenya. A quantitative research design using panel data analysis was used. The study adopted a census approach where 14 commercial banks having complete data for the period 2020–2024 were used. Secondary data was gathered from audited annual reports, financial statements, sustainability reports and publications by Central Bank of Kenya, using a structured data extraction template. Descriptive statistics (mean, standard deviation, minimum, maximum, skewness, and kurtosis) and inferential statistics (Pearson's correlation analysis and fixed-effects panel regression analysis) were used to analyse the data. The results showed that green bonds positively and statistically significantly influenced financial performance (β = 0.0905, p = 0.005). The results support the theoretical propositions of Institutional Theory. The study adds to literature by offering empirical evidence on the green bonds and financial performance relationship in the Kenyan banking context. The results can be used to develop policies on green finance adoption and sustainable banking. The commercial banks are urged to boost the issuance of green bonds to boost their profitability and promote environmental sustainability.

title: Mapping Digital Transformation, Innovation and Sustainability in European Union Countries
summary: Digital transformation, innovation and sustainability are important factors for the competitiveness and long-term development performance of a country. This study aims to compare the digital transformation, innovation and sustainability performance of the European Union countries and to reveal their similarities and differences. The Knowledge, Technology and Future Readiness dimensions of the IMD World Digital Competitiveness Index were used to represent digital transformation. For innovation, the Global Innovation Index was used and for sustainability, respectively, the SDG Index, Spillover indicator and Environmental Performance Index. The first analysis was made by the Multidimensional Scaling method and the structure obtained was tested for accuracy by the hierarchical clustering and the K-Means analysis. The findings reveal that the European Union countries are divided into three clusters for digital transformation, innovation and sustainability. The analysis results show a strong relationship between digital competitiveness and innovation performance while sustainability indicators show more limited differences between countries. It was also found that Northern and Western European countries have a similar and high performance in terms of digital transformation and innovation, and Eastern and Southern European countries have a relatively low performance.

title: Modeling national health supply chain resilience in Sub-Saharan Africa: an integrated system dynamics approach to routine healthcare and emergency preparedness
summary: Purpose This study aims to address important gaps in understanding public primary healthcare (PPHC) supply chain resilience in Sub-Saharan African (SSA) countries, with a focus on the complex interactions between routine healthcare delivery and emergency response during infectious disease outbreaks (IDOs). Design/methodology/approach The authors developed a system dynamics model, the health supply chain resilience (HSCR) model, to integrate epidemiological dynamics, supply chain operations and healthcare service delivery in SSA contexts. The model simulates the effects of IDOs on the interaction between routine and emergency healthcare delivery and evaluates supply chain preparedness strategies. Three types of interventions were assessed quantitatively: prepositioning of health commodities, local sourcing strategies and healthcare workforce expansion. Findings The analysis highlights the inherent trade-offs between emergency response and routine healthcare continuity. Combining complementary preparedness measures results in stronger resilience outcomes than individual interventions. The HSCR model supports the quantification of these trade-offs and the evidence-based prioritization of investments under resource constraints. Practical implications The model informs policymakers and healthcare professionals on how to design and prioritize supply chain preparedness strategies that balance emergency response and routine healthcare delivery. Originality/value This research contributes to the existing healthcare resilience literature as a novel tool to operationalize resilience, supporting evidence-based decision-making for health system stakeholders. It bridges theoretical and practical approaches to resilience-building in SSA national healthcare systems, offering a replicable model adaptable to diverse disease profiles and country settings, such as low- and middle-income countries with centralized PPHC systems.

title: Data-Driven Supply Chain Practice and Sustainable RMG Performance: The Mediating Roles of Organizational Agility and Eco-Efficiency Moderated by Green Absorptive Capacity
summary: Abstract Amidst rapid global scaling of Bangladesh's RMG industry, achieving sustainability via effective digital transformation unlocks immense potential for accelerating SDG goal attainment progress to ensure long-term competitiveness. Grounded in the Dynamic Capabilities View and Absorptive Capacity Theory, this research examines the mechanisms where data-driven supply chain practices (DDSCP) influence sustainable RMG performance (SRP) through the mediating role of organizational agility and eco-efficiency. Employing a quantitative, cross-sectional design, data from 215 supply chain and operational managers in Bangladesh were analyzed using PLS-SEM. The findings challenge deterministic technological narratives where DDSCP directly affects SRP and is notably minimal. Instead, the true value of digitalization is realized through the significant mediating roles of organizational agility and eco-efficiency. Importantly, while Green Absorptive Capacity directly enhances sustainable performance, it does not moderate the DDSCP-SRP relationship, acting as an independent operational baseline rather than a digital synergist in this developing context. This research advances supply chain literature by demonstrating that digital tools alone are insufficient, they require agile organizational reconfiguration and rigorous eco-efficient routines to achieve sustainable excellence. These insights provide actionable strategies for manufacturers and policymakers navigating stringent global compliance paradigms.

title: The Fourth Industrial Revolution. Social and economic impacts of the digital transformation
summary: Streszczenie Celem artykułu jest analiza wybranych społecznych i gospodarczych konsekwencji transformacji cyfrowej w Polsce oraz identyfikacja głównych szans, zagrożeń i nierówności związanych z rozwojem technologii cyfrowych i sztucznej inteligencji w obszarze komunikacji publicznej, rynku pracy i dobrostanu jednostki. Materiał i metody Artykuł ma charakter przeglądowy i diagnostyczny. Wykorzystano krytyczny przegląd literatury oraz analizę danych zastanych pochodzących z raportów Głównego Urzędu Statystycznego (GUS), Polskiego Instytutu Ekonomicznego (PIE), Naukowej i Akademickiej Sieci Komputerowej (NASK), Organizacji Współpracy Gospodarczej i Rozwoju (OECD) i Eurostatu, a także danych odnoszących się do poziomu cyfryzacji i wykorzystania AI w Polsce oraz Unii Europejskiej. Wyniki Analiza wskazuje na nierównomierny przebieg transformacji cyfrowej w Polsce. Rozwój usług cyfrowych dla konsumentów współistnieje z niższym wykorzystaniem zaawansowanych technologii w przedsiębiorstwach, szczególnie w sektorze MŚP. Transformacja zwiększa dostęp do informacji, automatyzację i możliwości komunikacji, ale wiąże się także z przeciążeniem informacyjnym, ryzykiem pogorszenia dobrostanu, polaryzacją rynku pracy i nierównym rozkładem kosztów społecznych. W komunikacji publicznej i instytucjach zwiększa znaczenie przejrzystości oraz kontroli, a dane NASK wskazują na intensywne korzystanie z internetu przez młodzież i trudności z ograniczeniem czasu korzystania z telefonu. Wnioski Ochrona indywidualnej autonomii wymaga rozwijania kreatywności, odporności poznawczej i krytycznej analizy informacji, a także przejrzystości w działaniu sztucznej inteligencji oraz odpowiedzialności instytucjonalnej. Sukces tej transformacji zależy od znalezienia równowagi między korzyściami gospodarczymi a dobrostanem społecznym.

title: Digital Transformation in Hospital Pharmacy Services: Effects on Team Performance
summary: Digital transformation has become a fundamental driver of healthcare innovation, particularly within hospital pharmacy services. Technologies such as electronic prescribing, barcode medication administration (BCMA), automated dispensing cabinets (ADCs), robotic dispensing systems, artificial intelligence (AI), clinical decision support systems (CDSS), and integrated pharmacy information systems have significantly reshaped pharmacy workflows. These innovations enhance medication safety, improve operational efficiency, and foster interdisciplinary collaboration. This review examines the influence of digital transformation on hospital pharmacy team performance, emphasizing productivity, communication, medication safety, workload distribution, and patient outcomes. Current evidence indicates that digital technologies reduce medication errors, increase dispensing accuracy, optimize inventory management, and improve staff satisfaction. Nevertheless, implementation challenges— including high costs, cybersecurity risks, resistance to organizational change, and training requirements—remain barriers to widespread adoption. Successful digital transformation requires strategic planning, continuous workforce education, leadership commitment, and robust evaluation metrics.

title: AI-driven FinTech and entrepreneurial financial agility in Pakistan: A moderated mediation model of intelligent financial analytics, automated FinTech services, AI readiness, and entrepreneurial performance
summary: Artificial intelligence is reshaping entrepreneurial financial management, yet its relationship with business performance in emerging economies remains insufficiently understood. Drawing on the dynamic capabilities view and the technology–organization–environment perspective, this study examines how intelligent financial analytics and automated FinTech services relate to entrepreneurial performance through financial agility, with AI readiness as a moderator. Online survey data from business owners, founders, and entrepreneurs in Islamabad and Rawalpindi, Pakistan, were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling. Both intelligent financial analytics and automated FinTech services were positively associated with financial agility and entrepreneurial performance. Financial agility partially mediated these relationships, while AI readiness strengthened the associations between both technologies and agility, as well as between agility and performance. Conditional indirect effects were greater at higher levels of readiness. These findings identify financial agility as a potential mechanism connecting financial technologies with entrepreneurial outcomes and highlight readiness as a boundary condition. The study suggests that entrepreneurs and policymakers should complement technology adoption with investments in digital infrastructure, data quality, employee skills, and leadership support for effective implementation.

title: Entrepreneurial intention, legal and institutional context, and corporate governance: Evidence from university students
summary: This study considers the broader institutional and legal framework that promotes responsible entrepreneurship while examining how attitudes toward entrepreneurship, subjective norms, and perceived behavioral control (PBC) affect entrepreneurial intention among economics and business students in Hanoi, Vietnam. It expands upon the theory of planned behavior (TPB) (Ajzen, 1991). The study used a quantitative technique using survey data from university students. The proposed correlations were examined using reliability analysis, exploratory factor analysis, and multiple linear regression. The findings indicate that entrepreneurial ambition is positively impacted by all three antecedents, with PBC being the most important predictor. In line with the TPB (Ajzen, 1991) and other entrepreneurship studies (Liñán & Chen, 2009), the results highlight the need for integrating entrepreneurial skills with enabling legal and governance frameworks. The study adds to the body of knowledge on entrepreneurship and corporate governance. It also offers useful implications for academic institutions and policymakers looking to improve entrepreneurship education, legal awareness, and responsible entrepreneurial behavior.

title: Digital Transformation, Cost-to-Income Ratio, and Profitability of Digital Banks in Indonesia
summary: Background: Digital banking has expanded rapidly in Indonesia, yet growth in assets and transaction activity has not consistently translated into stronger profitability. This tension raises the question of whether the transition to a digital operating model and the accompanying cost structure are associated with short-term financial performance. Objective: This study examines the relationship between post-digital-transformation status and bank profitability and separately evaluates the association between the Cost-to-Income Ratio (CIR) and Return on Assets (ROA). Method: The analysis uses an unbalanced panel comprising 79 valid bank-period observations drawn from quarterly reports of 10 Indonesian digital banks over 2019–2024. Panel-model selection relied on the Chow, Hausman, and Lagrange Multiplier tests, followed by diagnostic assessment and hypothesis testing. Results: Post-transformation status is negatively associated with ROA (B = -13.9108; p < 0.001). CIR also shows a negative association with ROA (B = -0.0525; p < 0.001). The estimates indicate that profitability remained under pressure during the observed transition period and that a heavier operating-cost burden corresponded with weaker asset returns. Conclusion: For the banks and periods observed, both digital-transformation status and higher CIR are associated with lower ROA. The findings highlight the importance of operating efficiency during digital transition, while the transformation coefficient should be interpreted as a short-term empirical association rather than evidence of a permanent causal effect.

title: STRATEGIC MANAGEMENT AND DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION: APPROACHES TO IMPROVING ORGANIZATIONAL PERFORMANCE
summary: This article examines the relationship between strategic management and digital transformation in contemporary organizations. The study considers how strategic planning, leadership, organizational culture, human capital, and performance measurement interact when organizations adopt digital technologies. A narrative review of established management literature is used to identify opportunities and limitations associated with digital transformation. The analysis suggests that technology investment alone does not guarantee organizational improvement; positive outcomes depend on strategic alignment, employee capabilities, process redesign, and continuous evaluation. An integrated conceptual framework is proposed to support responsible digital transformation and long-term organizational adaptability. The article provides practical recommendations for managers while distinguishing conceptual propositions from empirically tested findings.

title: Digital Transformation in Religious Public Administration: Policy Innovation for Inclusive Services
summary: Digital transformation can expand access to public services, yet fragmented administrative responsibilities and unequal digital capabilities may prevent users from benefiting from these changes. This study examines how policy innovation can connect institutional coordination and responsiveness to diverse user needs to support inclusive services in religious public administration. Adopting an interpretive approach, the study employs qualitative conceptual synthesis of theoretical contributions and published empirical research selected for their conceptual and substantive relevance. Analysis involves repeated reading, thematic interpretation, and comparison of concepts and arguments, guided by collaborative governance and public service logic. The synthesis indicates that policy innovation can support coordination by clarifying responsibilities, aligning procedures, and establishing arrangements for resolving problems across administrative units. Alongside these organizational arrangements, responsiveness requires attention to users’ ability to complete service processes and their opportunities to influence service decisions through accessible participation and appropriate assistance. Bringing these dimensions together suggests that identified barriers can inform procedural adjustment when connected to institutions with the authority and capacity to respond. Moreover, experiences of unsuccessful access provide relevant input for policy revision alongside feedback from users who complete services. The study proposes a conceptual model linking organizational capacity with user inclusion and offers guidance for reviewing service responsibilities, participation arrangements, and support mechanisms. These relationships remain propositions for empirical examination within public institutions administering religious affairs.

title: LEGAL FRAMEWORK FOR DATA AND ELECTRONIC TRANSACTIONS IN VIETNAM'S DIGITAL ECONOMY: CURRENT ISSUES AND DIRECTIONS FOR IMPROVEMENT
summary: In the context of the digital era and the Fourth Industrial Revolution, data has emerged as a strategic factor of production, while electronic transactions serve as the foundational mechanism underpinning the operation of the digital economy. However, the current legal framework still exhibits notable bottlenecks and regulatory gaps. This article examines the current state and proposes directions for improving the legal framework governing data and electronic transactions in Vietnam. Employing a qualitative legal research methodology combined with a Law and Economics approach, the study systematically analyzes normative legal documents and academic literature. The findings identify two major bottlenecks: first, the ambiguity surrounding the legal status of data and the structure of rights over data; and second, the lack of coherence between electronic transaction law and civil and commercial law, compounded by regulatory gaps regarding cross-border transactions. Accordingly, the paper highlights the urgent need to clarify the structure of legal rights, delineate the responsibilities of relevant stakeholders, and ensure systemic legal compatibility. This study provides a solid scientific and practical foundation for addressing institutional bottlenecks, unlocking data resources, and ensuring legal certainty, thereby contributing to the effective and sustainable development of Vietnam’s digital economy.

title: DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION, SME EXPORT COMPETITIVENESS, AND INDUSTRIAL UPGRADING: EVIDENCE FROM UZBEKISTAN'S MANUFACTURING SECTOR
summary: This study aims to investigate the influence of digital transformation on the export competitiveness and industrial upgrading of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) operating in Uzbekistan's manufacturing sector. The research will examine the adoption and utilization of digital technologies, including e-commerce platforms, digital payment systems, enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems, automation technologies, and data analytics. Export competitiveness will be assessed using indicators such as export intensity, export market diversification, product quality, delivery reliability, and buyer retention. Industrial upgrading will be evaluated across four dimensions: process upgrading, product upgrading, functional upgrading, and value chain upgrading. The study will employ a mixed-methods research design combining a survey of 350–450 manufacturing SMEs, semi-structured interviews, and an analysis of official statistical data. Quantitative data will be examined using regression analysis and structural equation modeling (SEM), while qualitative interview data will be analyzed through thematic analysis. According to the figures presented for 2025, SMEs accounted for 34.9% of Uzbekistan's industrial output and 36.6% of national exports, highlighting their significant contribution to the country's economic development. The study is expected to identify the mechanisms through which digital technologies contribute to export performance, examine the factors influencing their adoption, and propose policy and managerial measures to facilitate the transition of manufacturing SMEs toward higher-value-added activities.

summary: This article presents a systematic literature review on green finance and the econometrics of market risk. Amidst instability (specifically the COVID-19 pandemic), it analyzes hypotheses regarding the substitution and decoupling of traditional versus environmental assets. It justifies moving away from linear VAR models in favor of multiscale methods for assessing tail risks (such as wavelet analysis, cross-quantilograms, and quantile coherence). Systematizing these methods is crucial for enabling investors to hedge risks accurately and for improving the quality of state management regarding natural resource use.

title: UN SDG WITHIN CONTEMPORARY CORPORATE FINANCE: THE GAP BETWEEN DISCLOSURE AND CAPITAL ALLOCATION
summary: Problem setting. A decade after the adoption of the 2030 Agenda, companies have embedded sustainability principles into mainstream corporate reporting, while the financial effects of this transition remain considerably less certain. The growing financing needs associated with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), together with the recent weakening of several sustainable finance indicators, make it increasingly important to distinguish between declared corporate commitment and actual capital allocation. Aim. This study aims to assess this divergence, focusing on the relationship between SDG-related corporate commitments and observable financing and investment outcomes in contemporary corporate finance. Methodology. The study applies documentary, comparative, and structural-dynamic analysis to aggregate open-source data for 2015-2025 and examines five interconnected layers, namely, corporate disclosure, labelled debt issuance, sustainable fund flows, pricing signals, and real investment. Results. The results show that sustainability reporting has become near-universal among the world’s largest companies – 96% of the G250 report on sustainability; among G250 companies that report on sustainability or ESG matters, 74% use the SDGs. At the same time, sustainable bond issuance declined by 19% in 2025 to approximately USD 866 billion, while total global bond issuance increased by almost 11% to more than USD 10 trillion. Sustainable funds recorded USD 84 billion in net outflows in 2025, while SDG-related FDI in developing economies fell by 26% in 2024. Annual labelled issuance is equivalent in scale to approximately 20-25% of the estimated USD 4 trillion annual SDG financing gap, although this comparison does not measure actual gap coverage. The findings demonstrate a descriptive divergence between mature sustainability communication and several downstream indicators of financing and investment. Practical value. This study demonstrates that corporate treasurers, investors, regulators, and development finance institutions should assess disclosure, labelled instruments, investor commitments, and real investment separately when evaluating the financial contribution of business to the SDGs.

title: The Role of Artificial Intelligence in Administrative Decision-Making in Iraq: Digital Transformation as a Model
summary: This research aims to examine the role of artificial intelligence (AI) in enhancing the quality and efficiency of administrative decision-making in Iraq, adopting digital transformation as both an analytical model and an integrated practical framework. The study focuses on the readiness of Iraqi government institutions to adopt intelligent systems and the impact of these technologies on improving decision-making speed and transparency, reducing human error, and fostering a work environment grounded in data and intelligent analysis. The research employs a descriptive-analytical approach to review concepts related to AI and digital transformation, an inductive approach to infer relationships between variables, and a field-based approach involving the analysis of government documents and reports. Content analysis tools were also utilized to assess the extent to which AI applications—such as predictive systems, decision-support algorithms, chatbots, and big data analytics tools—are being employed. The findings indicate that the implementation of AI within Iraqi public administration remains in its early stages, despite official moves toward digitalization. Key opportunities identified include faster decision-making, increased transparency, reduced human intervention in routine tasks, and the creation of reliable databases to support planning and policymaking. Challenges include weak digital infrastructure, limited technical skills among staff, the absence of a legal framework regulating artificial intelligence applications, and poor integration between government systems. The research recommends formulating a comprehensive national strategy for artificial intelligence, developing digital infrastructure, upskilling government personnel, strengthening partnerships with the private sector and academic institutions, and updating legislation to align with digital governance and privacy protection standards, thereby ensuring a secure and effective environment for the adoption of smart technologies.

title: Sustainable finance versus non-sustainable finance and environmental sustainability: evidence from selected OECD economies
summary: This study aims to examine the role of sustainable finance vs. nonsustainable finance in environmental sustainability using OECD nations from 2012 to 2023. Surprisingly, the data characteristics provide a clear guide to choose an appropriate set of estimators. For instance, all variables are integrated at first difference, which compels this study to adopt the Johnson cointegration approach. In addition, to address cross-sectional dependence and serial correlation problems, this study employs the Driscoll-Kraay Standard Error estimator. To break the suspense, this study considers total factor productivity, urbanization, technology (including information & communication technology and artificial intelligence), green innovation, public‒private partnerships (PPPs), sustainability, and nonsustainable finance as environmental determinants. The obtained results remain fascinating for the specified nations. For instance, outcomes reveal an inverse relationship between total factor productivity, urbanization, and green innovations with carbon emissions. In addition, information and communication technology, artificial intelligence, and public‒private partnerships contribute to emissions. Similarly, sustainable finance (SF), including green bonds and green foreign direct investment, plays a significant role in addressing environmental issues. In contrast, nonsustainable finance increases emissions, except for financial stability and financial efficiency. Additionally, this study offers a moderate effect of SF on PPPs and green innovations, which does not support the sustainability theme. A heterogeneity view yields awe-inspiring results concerning environmental proxies, including CO2 emissions, ecological footprint, and load capacity factor. Finally, cross-country analysis describes fascinating outcomes under the proposed theme. Regarding outcomes, the present study offers imperative implications for becoming clean and green shortly.

title: The Impact of Process and Object Digital Transformation on the Moscow Exchange Index: A Textual Analysis of Patents
summary: The purpose of the study is to assess the association of process and object digital transformation with daily returns of the broad and sectoral Moscow Exchange indices using textual patent analysis. The subject is the short-run response of the Russian stock market to patent-based digital technology indicators. We propose a research method that separates object transformation (material components) from process transformation (management and information technologies). The empirical base contains 850,784 patent records covering the period from 1977 to 2025; the estimates use ARXEGARCH models. Conclusions: The association is heterogeneous across technology blocks and sectors: after multiple-testing correction, robust negative short-run coefficients remain for process indicators in energy and finance. The applied and empirical-methodological novelty of this study is a reproducible patent indicator of object and process digital transformation for the Russian stock market.

title: How does green intellectual capital influence reputational assets? From longitudinal dual-stage SEM-ANN perspective
summary: Purpose This study examines whether green intellectual capital enhances small and medium-sized enterprise reputation through environmental management accounting, addressing the imbalance between green investments and returns during China's manufacturing sector's low-carbon transition. It aims to position environmental management accounting as a mediator for reputational gains and sustainable financing. Design/methodology/approach Utilizing a dual-stage structural equation modeling-artificial neural network (SEM-ANN) approach, we analyzed longitudinal data from 442 Chinese manufacturing SMEs. Partial least squares-structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) assessed linear relationships, while ANN captured nonlinear patterns, with tenfold cross-validation ensuring robustness. Industry factors were controlled, and validated scales were employed. Findings All dimensions of green intellectual capital significantly boost SME reputation. Environmental management accounting (EMA) partially mediates this relationship, with green relational capital showing the strongest indirect effect (ß = 0.120). ANN revealed green structural capital's latent predictive power. EMA emerged as the dominant factor in reputation building. Practical implications SMEs should prioritize environmental management accounting for transparency and cost savings, invest in green relational capital and align green intellectual capital with accounting systems. Policymakers should incentivize adoption through tax subsidies and green certifications, fostering environmental accountability and global sustainability. Originality/value This study integrates conservation of resources theory with circular economic principles, introduces the first SEM-ANN hybrid framework in environmental management accounting and establishes a validated “green governance-disclosure-financing” cycle.

title: Agility as a capability amplifier: the co-evolution of organizational learning, big data and digital transformation in manufacturing
summary: Purpose Manufacturing firms face persistent digital upgrading bottlenecks, yet existing literature overlooks the co-evolutionary dynamics between organizational learning (OL), multi-dimensional data capabilities and agility in driving digital transformation (DT). This study aims to undertake a systematic empirical investigation of how OL (exploratory vs exploitative), big data capabilities (BDCs) and organizational agility (OA) synergistically shape the trajectory of DT. By synthesizing the Resource-Based View and Dynamic Capability Theory, this study further clarifies the mediating role of BDC dimensions and the boundary condition of OA in this process. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative research design was adopted using a structured questionnaire distributed to manufacturing managers across China. After a pre-survey validation, 505 valid responses were collected through online and offline channels. The proposed model was tested using partial least squares structural equation modeling via SmartPLS to examine direct, mediating and moderating effects. Findings Both exploratory and exploitative OL significantly advance DT, operating primarily through improvements in data analysis and integration capability and data application capability. OA positively moderates the impact of BDCs on transformation outcomes. Data acquisition capability alone shows no significant direct/indirect influence. Originality/value This study develops a framework that articulates the interactive mechanisms between OL, BDCs and agility in driving manufacturing DT, addressing the gap of treating these factors as isolated drivers in prior studies. This study empirically validates the differential mediating roles of three BDC dimensions and the moderating effect of agility.

title: A Review of Pension Systems, Institutional Dynamics, Corporate Governance and Pension Fund Performance: Evidence from Ghana and Global Perspectives
summary: This paper reviews pension systems, institutional dynamics, corporate governance, and pension fund performance with evidence from Ghana and global perspectives. The study adopts a qualitative and quantitative integrative review approach, synthesizing findings from multiple empirical and policy-oriented studies. The review highlights the global transition from pay-as-you-go defined benefit schemes toward multi-pillar systems that combine public and funded pension arrangements to improve sustainability and efficiency. Empirical evidence shows that pension fund performance is strongly influenced by corporate governance, institutional quality, and investment strategies. In Ghana, studies indicate that strong governance practices significantly enhance pension fund performance, while weak governance structures lead to inefficiencies and poor investment outcomes. Evidence also shows that pension fund assets have a strong positive relationship with Ghana’s GDP, explaining up to about 95% of economic variation in some models, highlighting the critical role of pension funds in economic development. The analysis further reveals that effective risk management and decentralized investment strategies improve returns, whereas conservative investment approaches limit performance. However, institutional weaknesses such as limited coverage, inadequate pension benefits, and sustainability challenges continue to constrain pension system effectiveness in Ghana. Overall, the findings suggest that pension fund performance is a function of governance quality, institutional strength, and strategic investment management. The paper concludes that achieving sustainable and efficient pension systems, particularly in emerging economies, requires integrated reforms aimed at strengthening governance structures, improving regulatory frameworks, and enhancing investment efficiency.

title: Digital Transformation of Nigerian Construction Industry Through BIM, AI, Digital Twins, IoT and Data Analytics
summary: This study assessed the digital transformation of construction processes with a view to developing an integrated framework for enhancing project performance in Abia State, Nigeria. The study was motivated by persistent time and cost overruns, poor quality, and fragmented paper-based processes in Nigeria’s SME-dominated construction industry, coupled with acute last-mile logistics challenges in Umuahia and Aba due to poor road networks and informal material delivery systems. Despite global advancement in Construction 4.0 driven by Building Information Modelling (BIM), Artificial Intelligence (AI), Digital Twins, Internet of Things (IoT) and Data Analytics, existing studies in Nigeria are fragmented, focusing mainly on BIM in Lagos/Abuja without integrating the five technologies, without linking to last-mile logistics, and without a mediated-moderated framework for South-East Nigeria.

title: DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION AND LAND ADMINISTRATION PERFORMANCE IN ANAMBRA STATE, NIGERIA: ASSESSING THE EFFECTS OF ADMINISTRATIVE AND TECHNOLOGICAL REFORMS
summary: Digital transformation promises improved land administration, yet technological adoption may coexist with administrative inefficiencies and uneven service outcomes. This study comparatively examined administrative efficiency, technological integration, and land administration performance in Anambra State, Nigeria. A descriptive and explanatory design combined a cross-sectional survey of 428 stakeholders with analysis of official administrative records covering 2012–2025. Survey responses were analysed using descriptive statistics and multiple regression, while administrative outputs were examined through trend analysis and percentage comparisons. Administrative efficiency and technological integration received mean ratings of 2.43 and 2.40, respectively, below the 2.50 agreement threshold. Both were positively associated with perceived performance: administrative efficiency recorded β = .245 (p < .001), compared with β = .148 (p = .001) for technological integration. The complete five-predictor institutional model explained 53.1% of performance variation, F(5,422) = 95.705 (p < .001). During 2012–2024, 8,048 Certificates of Occupancy were issued, averaging 619.08 annually, with an estimated increase of 63.98 certificates per year and compound annual growth of 13.40%. January–November 2025 issuance reached 3,688, exceeding the full-year 2024 total of 1,131. Related document outputs increased from 12,688 to 18,658 across these unequal observation periods, although category-level changes varied. The findings demonstrate that higher recorded productivity coexisted with unfavourable assessments of administrative and technological functioning. Sustainable transformation therefore requires procedural simplification, effective technological integration, staff development, and performance monitoring that combines output measures with service-quality indicators. The observational design supports comparative associations rather than causal attribution of performance changes to reforms

title: The Effect of Business Strategy, Profitability, Environmental Performance, and Corporate Social Responsibility on Firm Value
summary: This study aims to examine the effect of business strategy, profitability, environmental performance, and CSR on firm value in oil, gas, and coal subsector companies listed on Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) during 2019 – 2023. The methode used is a quantitative descriptive method. This research employs multiple linear regression analysis using SPSS 26 stratistical software. The research sample consists of 30 companies selected through a purposive sampling technique, resulting in 91 units of research data obtained from company’s annual financial reports published on IDX. The independent variables studied are business strategy, profitability, environmental performance, and corporate social responsibility, with leverage and liquidity as control variables. The results indicate that profitability and environmental performance have a positive significant effect on firm value, while business strategy and CSR not is not significantly affect firm value.

title: Can the Marketization of Data Elements Improve Forest Carbon Sink Efficiency? An Empirical Study from Hebei, China
summary: Under the “dual carbon” goals and the Digital China strategy, can marketizing data as a production factor effectively enhance forest carbon sink efficiency? This question is critical because the forestry sector remains a latecomer in data-driven transformation. This study utilizes panel data from 52 mountainous counties in Hebei Province (2007–2023) to construct an indicator system using the entropy method and the super-efficiency SBM-ML model. We then employ a two-fixed-effects model to empirically examine the impact of data element marketization (DEM) on forest carbon sink efficiency (FCSE) and its underlying mechanisms. The findings provide robust evidence that DEM is positively associated with FCSE, with a coefficient of 0.9507; this association is supported by a series of stability and endogeneity tests. Mechanism analysis suggests that DEM enhances FCSE by promoting forestry technology innovation; however, this positive effect weakens after green finance crosses the double thresholds of 0.0473 and 0.0971. Heterogeneity analysis indicates that the promotional effect of DEM is more pronounced in the Yanshan region of northern Hebei, as well as in digitally less advanced or environmentally more aware areas. Our findings underscore that advancing data element marketization in the forestry sector is not a standalone solution. It requires coordination with green finance regulation and adaptation to local conditions.

title: Managerial ability, narrative tone and state-designated vs. market-oriented media coverage
summary: This paper examines the relationship between managerial ability and the tone of corporate reporting narratives in Chinese listed firms’ Management Discussion and Analysis (MD&A) sections, and how this relationship varies with both state-designated media and market-oriented media coverage. This dichotomy between media outlets, together with the differences in linguistic practices by Chinese companies, relative to those in Anglo-Saxon territories, provide a rationale for our paper’s regional focus. We find that higher managerial ability is associated with a less optimistic tone in Chinese MD&A narrative disclosures, which augments prior evidence from narratives in voluntary earnings press releases. This negative relationship between managerial ability and MD&A narrative tone is stronger when a firm’s breadth of media coverage increases, indicating that the media plays a monitoring role in external corporate governance. However, this media coverage effect is conditional on the type of media. News coverage by state-designated media strengthens the negative association between managerial ability and MD&A narrative tone, but market-oriented media coverage has no significant effect. In addition, the effects are primarily driven by state-owned enterprises, highlighting the role of state-linked media governance in shaping corporate disclosure tone.

title: Hybrid Islamic-Conventional Banking Products Development: Integrating Complementary Banking Capabilities
summary: Islamic banking (IB) and conventional banking (CB) coexist in many financial systems, yet limited research explains how their complementary capabilities can be integrated into hybrid financial products while preserving Shariah requirements and institutional boundaries. This study proposes a seven-stage, problem-driven framework for hybrid IB-CB product development and demonstrates its application through three concepts: Tawazun SME capital, Baraka Green Finance, and Taaleem Fund, addressing SME financing, sustainable investment, and education financing, respectively. Expert evaluations from banking professionals and IB-CB specialists indicate that all three concepts were generally viewed positively, although assessments of collaboration potential were more cautious than evaluations of the concepts themselves. Among the proposed products, Tawazun SME capital exhibited the most balanced stakeholder value proposition, while Baraka Green Finance and Taaleem Fund were perceived as delivering stronger customer-oriented benefits. Qualitative findings highlight regulatory compatibility, independent Shariah governance, stakeholder alignment, operational readiness, and market awareness as critical conditions for successful implementation. The study contributes to the literature by providing a structured framework for transforming IB and CB complementarities into assessable hybrid product concepts. The findings offer practical insights for financial institutions seeking to expand innovation, promote financial inclusion, and facilitate collaboration across banking systems while preserving their distinct operational and regulatory characteristics.

title: Public technical disclosure of AI implementation in finance: Python-framed evidence from 253 NYSE-listed financial companies
summary: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) claims in public markets increasingly raise disclosure, comparability, and investor-protection questions, yet evidence on how listed financial firms publicly describe implementation remains fragmented and difficult to compare. This study examines public technical disclosure rather than internal adoption by constructing a screened, exchange-bounded corpus for 253 NYSE-listed financial companies. The source intake contained 554 rows; six exact repeated rows were removed before screening, leaving 548 screened rows. The 505-sentence extended analysis corpus combines a 253-sentence firm-anchor layer with a 252-sentence direct-verification layer; the remaining issuer is retained in the direct-verification audit as a closed unit with no strict direct match. Firms are coded into three disclosure states: explicit Python, indirect AI, and none, and the corpus is used to map subsector profiles, channel location, and the rarity of quantified public outcome claims through an outcome claims index (OCI). The results show that 34 firms (13.4%) are classified as Explicit Python, 216 (85.4%) as Indirect AI, and 3 (1.2%) as None. Explicit Python naming is uneven across subsectors and is concentrated mainly in employment materials and technical documentation rather than in filings or investor-facing channels. The public technical surface is therefore real but thin: firms more often signal implementation orientation than disclose a detailed tool stack. Quantified public outcome claims are rarer still, with five OCI-positive firms and five OCI-positive sentences (1.98% of firms). These findings indicate that public financial-sector communication is much stronger on AI-related implementation signals than on measurable outcomes. The paper offers a reproducible disclosure map for a bounded listed firm population and a framework for distinguishing general AI language, implementation-specific technical naming, and quantified public claims in regulated capital market settings.

title: A Conceptual Model for Revenue Diversification and Return on Equity Optimization in Banking
summary: This paper presents a critical, theory-grounded review of how revenue diversification shapes return on equity (ROE) in banking, and it develops an integrative conceptual model that links income mix, risk appetite, operating leverage, and institutional capability to sustainable performance. Rather than treating diversification as uniformly beneficial, the review applies a structured thematic synthesis of 250 sources, spanning income diversification theory, economies of scope, modern portfolio theory, and agency theory, to a core empirical literature of bank revenue mix and profitability published through 2024, supplemented by evidence on digital banking, fintech, and risk governance. The synthesis shows that non-interest income raises ROE only when it is matched to a bank's operational capability, funded within its risk appetite, and supported by governance that prices the associated volatility; where these conditions are absent, fee and trading income concentration erodes rather than strengthens returns. Beyond consolidating this evidence, the review's contribution is threefold: it reconciles the discrepant findings of the cross-country diversification literature with the largely disconnected single-market ROE-determinants literature; it specifies the conditions, technological, governance, and capital, under which diversification converts into higher risk adjusted ROE rather than higher earnings volatility; and it translates these conditions into four testable propositions and a practical measurement agenda for banks and regulators. Because the review is thematic rather than meta-analytic, it does not estimate a pooled effect size; its value lies instead in mapping where the evidence agrees, where it conflicts, and what a bank or regulator should measure next.

title: Steering and Setting Free: Insights From a 20‐Year Retrospective Case Study of a Security and Justice Organization's Digital Transformation
summary: ABSTRACT Advances in digital technologies are expected to fundamentally change how organizations operate and create value. Empirical studies show that public organizations face difficulties organizing and sustaining this digital transformation. To better understand these challenges, this study examines the organizational mechanisms underlying digital transformation in a public organization over the past 20 years. Our findings show that this transformation was primarily enabled by an emergent change approach, with influential planned changes occurring only occasionally. We identify the organizational mechanisms underlying both types of change and analyze their interdependence. Our findings suggest that both emergent and planned change approaches may be needed to enable digital transformation in public organizations effectively, but that combining them is complex in practice.

title: Audience-Contingent Reputation Effects: Signal Type, Expertise, and Investor Reactions to Management Guidance
summary: This study establishes that management reputation effects on investor reactions to guidance disclosures are co-determined by signal type and audience expertise—two dimensions that prior research has examined independently but never jointly theorized in a unified reputation framework. By showing that the same generic reputation signal carries positive valence among retail investors and negative valence among institutional investors—because expert audiences interpret its prominence as a substitute for rather than a complement to demonstrated forecasting competence—we demonstrate that reputation is not an intrinsic property of a signal but an emergent property of the signal–audience interaction

title: Развитие логистики и управления цепями поставок в сетевой розничной торговле в современных условиях
summary: Статья посвящена вопросам развития сетевой розничной торговли в современных условиях, характеризующихся неопределенностью логистики и проблемами управления цепями поставок на региональном уровне. Анализ оборота розничной торговли показал, что сетевые торговые компании усиливают свои позиции в сегменте продовольственных товаров, тогда как в общей рознице их доля несколько снижается. Выделены несколько ключевых векторов трансформации российского ритейла, которые формируют новую конкурентную реальность. Предложены технологии управления цепями поставок в условиях цифровой трансформации, которые дадут решающее конкурентное преимущество, предлагая клиентам принципиально новый уровень персонализированного и качественного обслуживания. The article is devoted to the development of online retail in modern conditions characterized by logistics uncertainty and supply chain management problems at the regional level. An analysis of retail trade turnover has shown that network trading companies are strengthening their positions in the food segment, while their share in general retail is slightly decreasing. Several key vectors of transformation of Russian retail have been identified, which form a new competitive reality. Supply chain management technologies in the context of digital transformation are proposed, which will give a decisive competitive advantage, offering customers a fundamentally new level of personalized and high-quality service.

title: Digital transformation and artificial intelligence in organic supply chains: A systematic review with insights from South Tamil Nadu
summary: Organic agriculture is growing rapidly in India, yet organic supply chains remain structurally fragmented, particularly in smallholder-dominated regions such as South Tamil Nadu. Digital transformation and artificial intelligence (AI) offer promising solutions to persistent challenges, including inadequate cold-chain infrastructure, limited traceability, intermediary-dependent marketing and certification workflow inefficiencies. This systematic review draws on evidence from 30 peer-reviewed and institutional publications. These sources were identified through a PRISMA-compliant search of Scopus, Elsevier, Taylor & Francis, Web of Science, IEEE, MDPI, Wiley, FAO, and government databases. The findings indicate that AI-enabled precision farming, machine learning-based demand forecasting, Internet of Things-enabled cold-chain monitoring, and blockchain-supported traceability improve production efficiency, market access and organic supply chain transparency. However, widespread adoption is constrained by inadequate rural connectivity, limited digital literacy, incompatibility between digital platforms and Participatory Guarantee System certification workflows, and weak first-mile infrastructure. This review proposes the Digital Transformation and AI Readiness Framework for Organic Supply Chains (DARF-OSC). DARF-OSC is a five-stage conceptual model that integrates Diffusion of Innovations theory with the Resource-Based View. Also, this review identifies five key research gaps and tiered policy recommendations for South Tamil Nadu.

title: Assessment of Cybersecurity Risks in the Logistics Sector Using Fuzzy AHP Methodology
summary: Cybersecurity is the sum of processes, policies, and technical measures applied against threats to information and communication infrastructure. With the digital transformation movements across all sectors, the importance of cybersecurity is increasing day by day. The aim of this study is to identify the cybersecurity risks arising in the intensive use of digital technologies in logistics operations and to determine the importance of these risks. A comprehensive literature review was conducted to identify cybersecurity risks in logistics. Eight cybersecurity risk criteria were validated based on expert opinions. The Fuzzy AHP method was used to determine the importance levels of the identified risks. To meet the criteria, an adjustment formula with a 1-7 Saaty view was prepared and developed by five IT specialists working in the logistics sector. The collected data was combined and analyzed using transformed matrices. As a result of the analyses, an importance ranking was obtained for the 8 criteria. According to the research, the top three cybersecurity risks are: Ransomware Attack Risk, Risks Arising from Supply Chain Stakeholders, and Attack Risks on Customs and Port Systems. The sum of the importance levels of these three risks is approximately 65%.

title: From Green Human Resource Management Practice to Environmental Performance
summary: This study examines how green human resource management (GHRM) relates to green knowledge management (GKM), environmental awareness (EA), green innovation (GI), and environmental performance (EP), which refer to as an application of human resource strategy in an organization that does not cause negative impact to the environment. The study employed the quantitative approach by completion of a questionnaire by 406 human resource supervisors, managers, and directors from chain hotels located in different regions of Thailand. Findings revealed that GHRM is related to GKM which is the factor influencing EA and EP, indicating that EA plays a key role in translating environmental knowledge into innovation and performance. The hospitality industry is seeking to improve environmental performance by treating GHRM as an integrated set of practices. Green Human resource management influences on environmental factors becomes a continuous behavior which recognizes the organization's environmental impact and addresses or enhances relevant knowledge and technology to improve employee performance.

title: Digital transformation, dynamic capabilities and ESG performance: post-TCFD UK evidence
summary: Purpose This study examines how digital transformation (DT) affects environmental, social, and governance (ESG) performance and whether exploitative and explorative DT contribute differently under the UK's post- Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures (TCFD) regime. Design/methodology/approach Grounded in Ambidexterity Theory and Dynamic Capability Theory (DCT), the study constructs firm-level DT and ESG measures from unstructured annual and sustainability disclosures using a Natural Language Processing (NLP)–Entropy framework. Panel data for Financial Times Stock Exchange (FTSE)-listed non-financial firms (2020–2024) are analysed using fixed-effects regressions with firm-clustered standard errors. Mediation tests evaluate CSR and total factor productivity (TFP) as capability-based mechanisms. Findings DT is positively associated with ESG performance. Both exploitative and explorative DT exhibit significant positive relationships with ESG, indicating that ambidextrous digitalisation supports sustainability improvements. Mediation via CSR and TFP is statistically weak, suggesting that the DT–ESG linkage is not transmitted through these proxies within the study horizon and may operate primarily through direct digital mechanisms. Research limitations/implications The study focuses on FTSE non-financial firms and a five-year window, which may constrain generalisability and the detection of longer-run capability maturation. Future work should extend the time horizon, employ alternative capability measures, and apply stronger causal identification designs. Practical implications Firms can improve ESG outcomes by pursuing both exploitative and explorative digital initiatives, while policymakers can reinforce gains by strengthening disclosure quality and digital reporting infrastructures. Originality/value The study integrates digital ambidexterity and DCT, introduces an NLP–Entropy measurement approach for DT and ESG, and provides evidence from a disclosure-intensive UK setting.

title: Corporate Governance in India: Challenges and the way Forward
summary: Corporate governance is the machine through which organizations are directed, controlled, monitored and held accountable to their shareholders and different stakeholders. In India, corporate governance has evolved considerably via an aggregate of regulation, securities regulation, judicial decisions and institutional reforms. The groups Act, 2013 brought a comprehensive statutory framework handling directors' duties, independent directors, board committees, related-celebration transactions, company social duty, monetary reporting and managerial duty. For listed entities, the Securities and trade Board of India ("SEBI") has supplemented this framework via the Securities and exchange Board of India (list duties and Disclosure requirements) regulations, 2015 ("LODR guidelines"). No matter this significant regulatory framework, good sized demanding situations stay. Corporate governance failures may additionally rise up from promoter dominance, inadequate independence of boards, useless audit mechanisms, related-birthday celebration transactions, insufficient protection of minority shareholders, accounting irregularities, statistics asymmetry, weak whistle-blower mechanisms and the gap between formal compliance and major governance.
