title: Fiscal–ESG governance coherence: Examining regulatory fragmentation in Indonesia’s sustainability governance
summary: As sustainability increasingly shapes governance and accountability agendas, the relationship between fiscal policy and environmental, social, and governance (ESG) frameworks warrants closer examination. This study examines how taxation and sustainability are framed within Indonesia's fiscal and sustainable finance regulatory frameworks, focusing on the explicit linkage between fiscal contribution and ESG accountability. It applies qualitative document analysis and abductive thematic analysis to Indonesia's Tax Harmonization Law, the Sustainable Finance Roadmap Phase II, and OJK Regulation No. 51 of 2017. Documents were manually coded and analyzed across three dimensions: institutional mandate, policy instrument, and evaluative alignment. The findings show that taxation is framed primarily around fiscal resilience and development financing, whereas ESG governance emphasizes risk management and disclosure-based accountability. Although both domains address aspects of sustainability, the regulatory instruments examined establish limited explicit connections between taxation and ESG governance, particularly regarding the inclusion of fiscal contribution in ESG evaluative mechanisms. This indicates a gap in regulatory alignment, rather than demonstrating complete separation in practice. The study introduces Fiscal–ESG Governance Coherence as an analytical lens for assessing fiscal-sustainability alignment across institutional mandate, policy instrument, and evaluative mechanism at the regulatory design level. The findings highlight opportunities to strengthen the relationship between fiscal accountability and sustainability governance.

title: Economic impacts of subsea cable deployment
summary: This paper provides a comprehensive empirical analysis of the economic impact of submarine cable (SMC) infrastructure, which is critical for global digital connectivity and carries almost all intercontinental data traffic. Despite their fundamental role in the digital economy, robust evidence on the economic returns of SMC investments is very scarce. To address this, we use a panel dataset of developed countries and causal identification strategies, such as two-way fixed effects models and instrumental variables exploiting exogenous variation from factors like a country's coastline length and legacy market competition. In our empirical analysis we first describe how international bandwidth (IBW) can be used as a proxy for SMC capacity and examine how it affects domestic broadband quality levels. We then quantify the impact on broadband demand, finding distinct yet robust demand elasticities for mobile and fixed services. We find that a 1% increase in IBW drives an increase in mobile broadband adoption between 0.049% and 0.081%, while the increase for fixed broadband adoption ranges between 0.056% and 0.061%. Finally, we translate these estimates into a simple cost-benefit framework using an illustrative transatlantic cable project connecting Ireland and the United States. This analysis shows that the substantial GDP spillovers overwhelmingly exceed the total private deployment costs. Our findings affirm that SMC deployments generate significant positive externalities and high social returns. While it has been argued in the previous literature that these effects are critical to developing nations lacking infrastructure, our findings indicate this effect is also applicable to advanced economies. Consequently, we argue that policymakers in coastal nations, regardless of their level of development, have a strong economic incentive to facilitate private investment by reducing regulatory barriers and transaction costs associated with, for example, cable permits and landing stations.

title: Bringing Organization Back In: Rethinking Technology–Organization Nexus in Digital Government
summary: Digital government scholarship has become increasingly sophisticated about technology, yet surprisingly thin about organization. Recent studies have shown how algorithms shape administrative discretion, how artificial intelligence changes public decision-making, and how digital systems affect frontline work, accountability, and public values. These advances matter. But they also reveal a conceptual imbalance. Too often, digital transformation is treated as the introduction of a new technology into an otherwise stable administrative setting. When performance changes, the technology receives the explanatory credit; when implementation fails, organizational capacity is added as a contextual condition. This perspective argues for a different starting point: digital government should be understood as a process of organizational transformation produced through the interaction between technology and organization. Put simply, we need to bring organization back into digital government research.

title: The Relationship Between Digitalization, Sustainable Development and Government Effectiveness in OECD Countries
summary: This study examines the impact of digitalization on sustainable development in OECD countries over the period 2000–2024. Digitalization is measured through a composite index constructed by Principal Component Analysis (PCA) using internet usage, fixed broadband subscriptions, and mobile cellular subscriptions. The Sustainable Development Goals Index (SDGI) is employed as the indicator of sustainable development. Gross domestic product per capita, trade openness, and government effectiveness are included as control variables. The empirical analysis is conducted using the Driscoll–Kraay estimator and panel quantile regression approach. The findings indicate that digitalization exerts a positive and statistically significant effect on sustainable development. Furthermore, the quantile regression results reveal that the impact of digitalization becomes stronger in countries with higher levels of sustainable development performance. These findings suggest that digital transformation constitutes an important driver of sustainable development; however, its effectiveness varies according to countries’ institutional and economic capacities. By employing a PCA-based digitalization index and examining heterogeneous effects across different levels of sustainable development, the study provides new empirical evidence for the OECD countries.

title: AI Adoption and Dynamic Capabilities in Chinese SMEs: the Mediating Role of Digital Entrepreneurial Orientation—A Conceptual Framework
summary: This paper develops a conceptual framework that examines how artificial intelligence (AI) adoption may influence dynamic capabilities in Chinese small and mediumsized enterprises (SMEs), with digital entrepreneurial orientation (DEO) as a proposed mediating mechanism. Drawing on dynamic capabilities theory and the digital entrepreneurship literature, the paper argues that AI adoption does not automatically translate into dynamic capabilities. Rather, AI adoption may foster DEO—comprising digital innovativeness, digital proactiveness, and digital risktaking—which in turn may help firms sense opportunities, seize them, and reconfigure resources. Three testable propositions are developed. The framework contributes to dynamic capabilities theory by specifying DEO as a strategic mediating pathway through which AI resources may be converted into organizational capabilities. It also offers implications for SME managers and policymakers seeking to support digital transformation under resource constraints.

title: Energy Policy and Energy Management in China: Governance Logic and Future Pathways of Structural Transformation
summary: China’s energy policy and management are transitioning from scale expansion to systemic restructuring. During the 14th Five-Year Plan period (2021–2025), renewables accounted for approximately 60% of installed capacity, and the Energy Law took effect. Entering the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026–2030), binding targets require non-fossil energy to reach 25% of primary consumption and 50% of electricity generation. Meanwhile, the management system is shifting from dual control over energy consumption to dual control over carbon emissions. This paper examines China’s energy governance transition across three dimensions: policy evolution, management challenges, and institutional restructuring. In terms of policy, the 14th Five-Year Plan saw accelerated green transition, while the 15th centers on carbon peaking, shifting from scale to structure-orientation, and from policy-driven to rule-of-law-based governance. In terms of management, four challenges emerge, including tensions among security, low-carbon, and economic objectives, bottlenecks in new energy integration, social costs of transitioning traditional energy roles, and governance hurdles in digital transformation, revealing structural barriers to policy implementation. In terms of institutional restructuring, rule of law, marketization, and systematization are advancing in parallel, shaping the institutional framework for governance modernization. Looking ahead, computing-energy coupling, zero-carbon industrial park experiments, and international governance dimensions are emerging as frontier issues. This paper argues that China’s energy transition is not merely technological or industrial, but a fundamental shift in governance logic. The modernization of governance capacity, rather than unidimensional gains in installed capacity or technical metrics, determines the transition’s success. The deep shift from scale expansion to systemic restructuring, and from administrative dominance to institutional governance, will shape the future of China’s energy development.

title: Research on public trust repair paths of corporate social responsibility visual narratives in crisis public relations contexts
summary: In the context of crisis public relations, corporate social responsibility visual narrative has become an important way for corporations to respond to public doubt, explain responsibility relations, and rebuild public trust. Compared with written statements, audiovisual texts can transform corporate responsibility into a more perceptible narrative experience through shot organization, character presentation, scene arrangement, and emotional rhythm. Based on CSR videos publicly released after corporate crises from 2020 to 2024, visual text coding, questionnaire experiments, and statistical analysis are combined to examine the effects of visual authenticity, responsibility recognition, emotional resonance, and action commitment on public trust repair. The results show that the narrative path composed of factual explanation, responsibility recognition, and action evidence has a stronger trust repair effect. Responsibility recognition and action commitment have more prominent effects on public trust. Emotional narrative can increase viewing involvement, but its trust repair effect remains limited when responsibility explanation and remedial action are absent. These findings indicate that post crisis CSR videos should not remain at the level of public welfare display and emotional appeal. They should build a more credible visual communication path through clear factual response, visible responsibility assumption, and sustained action evidence.

title: A Kaizen perspective for managing human-technology continuous improvement in the digital age
summary: Purpose The paper examines how digital technologies are transforming continuous improvement (CI) by altering the cognitive and relational dynamics that have long underpinned Kaizen-oriented learning. Design/methodology/approach This paper adopts a conceptual approach, drawing on insights from CI, organizational learning and digital transformation. It establishes an interpretive framework focusing on cognitive offloading as a pivotal mechanism connecting technology adoption with the decline of participatory improvement routines. Findings Digital technologies can significantly speed up decision-making and streamline processes. However, there is a downside: their widespread use may reduce our ability to reflect, learn from experience and solve problems. When we start relying too much on technology for cognitive tasks, we risk becoming efficient in a procedural sense but socially vulnerable. This can weaken human skills that are essential for viable improvement. Practical implications The paper presents a conceptual model and practical guidelines for managers interested in developing CI systems that focus on maintaining discretion, fostering a strong learning environment and encouraging collective sense-making instead of merely optimizing execution. Originality/value Thanks to the adoption of Kaizen principles, the paper advances the discussion on CI by highlighting the fact that cognitive offloading poses a risk not only to individuals but also to organizations, particularly in environments that rely heavily on digital technology.

title: Sustainable Development Through Carbon Net‐Zero Strategies: Analyzing External and Internal Factors, Corporate Carbon Accounting, and Scope 3 Emissions Reduction
summary: ABSTRACT This study examines how external pressures and internal corporate drivers shape the adoption of carbon accounting practices and their effectiveness in reducing Scope 3 greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions among leading European companies. Drawing data from 90 European companies recognized as climate reporting pioneers in the CDP database, the study tests five hypotheses and develops a framework linking governance and strategic management factors to Scope 3 emissions outcomes. Original data from annual and sustainability reports provide the empirical foundation for this analysis. The findings reveal that Scope 3 emissions have not declined significantly in recent years, largely due to inadequate policy and regulatory guidance. Nevertheless, the study identifies a meaningful correlation between carbon performance and the pursuit of proactive carbon strategies. These results underscore the need for transparent sustainability reporting standards and accessible climate data to accurately evaluate corporate carbon strategies. Furthermore, the study highlights how external pressures and internal corporate ambitions jointly shape organizational goal setting and drive the adoption of carbon accounting practices, which ultimately improve environmental performance and support sustainable development.

title: Role of the digital specialist community public health nurse: reimagining community nursing in the AI-enabled public health landscape
summary: Digital transformation and artificial intelligence are redefining how people access and navigate community healthcare. Concurrently, community nursing services are facing a sustained workforce decline. While digital nurse leadership has matured in many acute organisations, community nurses are increasingly expected to deliver technology-enabled care without equivalent leadership structures, support or career pathways. In this article, the author details a proposal for a digital specialist community public health nurse (digital SCPHN) role framework. The author describes the digital SCPHN as first and foremost a clinician, with digital capability as an essential enhancement rather than a replacement of core nursing objectives. Positioned as a digital translator and champion within community teams, the digital SCPHN helps people to navigate complex digital healthcare systems while supporting their colleagues through technology-enabled care prioritisation, secure safeguarding communication and community risk insight. The author also outlines six actionable recommendations for front-line nurses, team leads and system commissioners to strengthen community nursing impact, improve digital literacy and ensure equitable, person-centred care in digitally enabled neighbourhood healthcare systems.

title: Pengaruh Accrual Earnings Management dan ESG disclosure terhadap Capital Structure: Studi pada Perusahaan Non-keuangan yang Terdaftar di Bursa Efek Indonesia
summary: Studi ini bertujuan menganalisis pengaruh accrual earnings management dan ESG disclosure terhadap capital structure di perusahaan non-keuangan yang terdaftar di BEI periode 2020-2024. Studi ini mempergunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan data sekunder dan teknik purposive sampling. Analisis dilaksanakan mempergunakan regresi linear. Temuan studi ini memperlihatkan bahwasanya accrual earnings management dan ESG disclosure dapat memengaruhi signifikan negatif terhadap capital structure. Temuan tersebut memperlihatkan bahwasanya perusahaan yang menerapkan manajemen laba serta mempunyai tingkat pengungkapan ESG lebih tinggi cenderung mempunyai tingkat leverage lebih rendah. Studi ini memberikan bukti empiris yang dapat memperkaya literatur bidang akuntansi dan keuangan, sekaligus menjadi bahan pertimbangan bagi perusahaan menetapkan kebijakan pendanaan optimal. Implikasi penelitian menunjukkan pentingnya transparansi informasi dan kualitas pelaporan keuangan dalam mendukung Keputusan pendanaan. Hasil penelitian ini juga dapat menjadi referensi bagi investor, manajemen, dan pemangku kepentingan dalam mengevaluasi risiko keuangan, tata kelola, serta strategi perusahaan secara lebih komprehensif dan berkelanjutan untuk menghadapi perubahan lingkungan bisnis global.

title: Digital-Based Teacher Human Resource Management for Educational Transformation Readiness
summary: This study aims to analyze and develop a digital-based teacher human resource (HR) management model to strengthen teachers’ readiness for educational transformation. This study employed a qualitative case study design to examine the implementation of digital-based HR management in a madrasah. Data were collected through in-depth interviews, participatory observations, and document review with the madrasah principal, curriculum representative, and teachers. We ensured data credibility through source and method triangulation. Data analysis involved condensing, displaying, and verifying data, supported by thematic analysis. The findings indicate that teacher HR management has begun integrating digital technology into professional development, work processes, and educational management, but implementation remains only partially institutionalized. Teachers’ readiness for transformation depends on digital literacy, ongoing professional development, leadership support, and the availability of institutional systems. The findings further reveal that a shared digital organizational culture has not yet fully formed, so technology use and innovation remain partly dependent on individual initiatives. The study suggests that sustainable educational transformation requires an integrated, digital-based HR management model supported by continuous professional development, structured digital systems, visionary leadership, and a collaborative, adaptive organizational culture. Such integration can strengthen teachers’ capacity and institutional readiness to respond effectively to ongoing digital transformation.

title: Peningkatan Aksesibilitas UMKM Desa Wonosari Melalui Pemetaan Lokasi Usaha Berbasis Google Maps
summary: Many Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) in rural areas still face challenges regarding conventional marketing and limited location accessibility due to a lack of digital registration on online maps. This community service initiative aims to enhance the accessibility and visibility of MSMEs in Wonosari Village through a Google Maps-based business location mapping program. The methodology employed combines participatory and educational approaches, involving outreach, intensive door-to-door training, assistance with registering location coordinates, and periodic monitoring. Collected business data—including business names, categories, full addresses, contact details, and product photos—was submitted for direct verification by Google. Program evaluations revealed a 40% average increase in the partners' digital marketing knowledge, based on pre-test and post-test results. MSME locations were successfully mapped with precision on Google Maps, significantly making it easier for consumers from outside the area to locate the physical business premises. Discussions highlighted that integrating digital visibility via Google Maps complements user-friendly physical accessibility, expands market reach, boosts sales potential, and shifts the rural business owners' mindset regarding the ease of adopting digital technology. The program has proven effective in accelerating digital transformation and sustainably supporting rural economic self-reliance.

title: A Multidimensional Analysis of the Relationship between Earnings Management and Financial Statement Reporting Quality among Deposit Money Banks in Nigeria
summary: This study examined the relationship between earnings management and financial statement reporting quality among Deposit Money Banks (DMBs) in Nigeria over the period 1994–2024. Specifically, it examined the relationship between discretionary accruals and accrual quality; loan loss provisions and accounting conservatism; earnings smoothing and earnings persistence; real earnings management and earnings predictability; discretionary loan loss provisions and transparency and disclosure; and income-increasing/decreasing accruals and the value relevance of financial statements. Anchored on agency theory, the study adopted an ex-post facto research design and employed panel least squares regression using a balanced panel of 17 purposively selected DMBs, comprising 527 bank-year observations. Panel unit-root tests indicated that the study variables were stationary, while the Kao residual cointegration test indicated a long-run relationship among the variables. The findings revealed a statistically significant positive relationship between discretionary accruals and accrual quality (p = 0.0081), a statistically significant negative relationship between loan loss provisions and accounting conservatism (p = 0.0130), and a statistically significant negative relationship between income-increasing/decreasing accruals and the value relevance of financial statements (p = 0.0364). However, no statistically significant relationship was found between earnings smoothing and earnings persistence (p = 0.6375), real earnings management and earnings predictability (p = 0.1083), or discretionary loan loss provisions and transparency and disclosure (p = 0.2193). The study concludes that the relationship between earnings management and financial statement reporting quality varies across the six dimensions examined among Nigerian DMBs. It recommends strengthened regulatory monitoring of discretionary accruals and loan loss provisioning, improved internal controls, enhanced board and audit committee oversight, and more transparent disclosure of accounting estimates to mitigate opportunistic earnings management and strengthen financial statement reporting quality in the Nigerian banking sector.

title: Dual Status Signaling and the Diffusion of Green Innovation
summary: This paper examines how status signaling shapes the diffusion of sustainable technologies. We develop an agent-based model that integrates two distinct forms of social status: conspicuous consumption, associated with traditional wealth-oriented prestige, and conspicuous conservation, reflecting the social value attached to visible sustainable choices. Heterogeneous consumers interact with strategically adapting firms that differentiate products along environmental and prestige dimensions. Calibrated to the German electric vehicles market, the model reproduces qualitative diffusion patterns and shows how diffusion accelerates when green innovations simultaneously signal material prestige and environmental values. The results further demonstrate how the effectiveness of this mechanism depends on structural conditions such as the income distribution and market structure.

title: MANAGEMENT OF ORGANIZATIONAL MARKETING COMMUNICATIONS IN THE CONTEXT OF DIGITALIZATION: AN INTEGRATED APPROACH
summary: The article examines an integrated approach to managing organizational marketing communications under digital transformation. It substantiates that digitalization changes traditional communication models, expands stakeholder interaction channels, and increases the need to combine analytical and generative tools. The purpose of the study is to analyze the theoretical foundations and practical aspects of integrated marketing communication management in public administration bodies and nonprofit organizations, including sports organizations. The study analyzes Big Data, CRM systems, social media, AI-generated content, and chatbots in communication activities. The study compares objectives, audiences, channels, digital tools, challenges, and ethical risks. The components of an integrated approach are proposed: consistency of information messages, multichannel communication, orientation toward target audience needs, and continuous feedback. It is established that CRM systems support stakeholder relationship management, personalized interaction, and communication performance analysis; Big Data expands opportunities for audience segmentation and behavioral analysis; and generative artificial intelligence facilitates adaptive content creation and communication automation. Digital integration increases audience trust and engagement, optimizes expenditures, and enables faster responses to environmental changes. The effectiveness of integrated communications depends on the consistency of messages across different channels and their adaptation to the specific needs of stakeholder groups. The systematic combination of digital technologies with traditional communication tools is substantiated as a basis for organizational resilience in a dynamic environment. Ethical, reputational, institutional, and resource-related challenges associated with disinformation, non-transparent use of AI, personal data protection, unequal digital skills, and limited resources are systematized. The scientific novelty lies in conceptualizing an integrated approach as a universal yet sector-differentiated model for managing organizational marketing communications. The practical value lies in applying the model to improve communication strategies.

title: TARGETED EVALUATION OF HIGHER EDUCATION INSTITUTION EFFICIENCY BASED ON A DIGITAL STRATEGIC MANAGEMENT MODEL AND SYSTEMIC INTEGRAL INDEX
summary: In the contemporary landscape of global higher education, the accelerating pace of digital transformation necessitates a paradigm shift from traditional intuition-driven administration to rigorous, metricsbased, and data-driven management models. This study explores the methodology for a comprehensive, multilayered, and systematic assessment of the strategic development potential of higher education institutions (HEIs) operating within dynamic socioeconomic environments. To bridge the gap between fragmented functional metrics and holistic institutional oversight, we develop a new mathematical-methodological framework designated as the Systemic Strategic Development Integral Index (SSDI). The SSDI compiles 15 highly specialized primary metrics structured across five fundamental institutional dimensions: Educational Quality (EQ), Scientific-Innovative Activity (SIA), Digital Maturity (DM), Financial Sustainability (FS), and External Cooperation (EC). To achieve a unified scalar metric from disparate units of measurement, a min-max linear normalization algorithm is combined with weight assignment protocols via the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP). The operational viability and empirical sensitivity of the model are validated through multi-scenario predictive forecasting models tracking index trajectories for the period 2026–2030 across five structurally diverse higher education institutions. The empirical simulations demonstrate that accelerating comprehensive digital interoperability—under an optimistic governance framework—can catalyze a 35% to 40% enhancement in net institutional efficiency. This index provides university boards, ministries of education, and executive leadership teams with a scalable diagnostic tool to locate systemic vulnerabilities, optimize resource allocation, and scientifically validate mid-to-long-term strategic pathways.

title: Assessment of the efficiency of resource potential utilization in the agricultural sector of the economy under investment and innovation development
summary: Ukraine’s agricultural sector is undergoing transformation under the influence of wartime challenges, economic restructuring, European integration, digitalization, and the growing need for sustainable resource management. Improving the efficiency of resource potential utilization has become a prerequisite for strengthening the competitiveness and sustainability of agricultural enterprises. The purpose of this study is to provide a comprehensive assessment of the efficiency of resource potential utilization in the agricultural sector of the economy under investment and innovation development and to substantiate organizational and economic measures for its improvement. The research is based on a systems approach using economic-statistical, comparative, analytical, economic-mathematical, graphical, forecasting, and composite assessment methods. The empirical analysis covers agricultural enterprises in the Poltava region during 2015–2025. Resource potential utilization efficiency was comprehensively assessed by integrating economic, investment, innovation, environmental, and managerial indicators. The results show that technological modernization, digital transformation, investment activity, and strategic management are the principal drivers of efficient resource utilization and sustainable enterprise development. An integrated organizational and economic model for resource potential development is proposed, combining precision agriculture, digital monitoring, resource-saving technologies, and human capital development. Forecasting confirms the positive impact of the proposed measures on labour productivity, capital productivity, profitability, investment activity, digitalization, and the integrated indicator of resource utilization efficiency. The scientific novelty lies in improving a comprehensive methodological approach to assessing the efficiency of resource potential utilization in the agricultural sector of the economy through integrating economic, investment, innovation, environmental, and managerial components. The practical significance lies in applying the proposed approach to strategic planning for agricultural enterprise development, investment decision-making, and improving resource management efficiency.

title: AI-DRIVEN ONLINE ADAPTIVE LEARNING SYSTEMS IN HIGHER EDUCATION: AN INTEGRATIVE REVIEW OF LEARNER MODELLING, ADAPTATION MECHANISMS AND EVIDENCE OF EFFECTIVENESS
summary: The rapid expansion of online and blended learning in higher education has exposed a persistent limitation of conventional online courses: content is delivered to all students in the same sequence and at the same pace, regardless of differences in prior knowledge, learning progress and needs. Online adaptive learning systems, increasingly powered by artificial intelligence (AI), aim to overcome this limitation by continuously diagnosing the learner and personalising content, sequence, difficulty and feedback. Aim. This article reviews the theoretical foundations, learner-modelling techniques, adaptation mechanisms and empirical evidence on the effectiveness of AI-driven online adaptive learning systems, and derives implications for higher education systems undergoing digital transformation, with particular reference to Uzbekistan. Methods. An integrative literature review was conducted following the framework of Whittemore and Knafl. Seminal works and peer-reviewed publications indexed in Scopus, Web of Science, ERIC and Google Scholar, together with international policy documents, were analysed using reflexive thematic synthesis. Results. Six themes were identified: (1) pedagogical and psychological foundations; (2) learner modelling, from Bayesian knowledge tracing to deep learning; (3) adaptation targets and mechanisms; (4) evidence of effectiveness from meta-analyses; (5) the emerging role of generative AI; and (6) ethical, pedagogical and infrastructural challenges. Meta-analytic evidence shows moderate to large positive effects of intelligent and adaptive tutoring on learning outcomes, while gaps remain regarding teacher involvement, transparency and applicability to low-resource language contexts. Conclusion. Effective adaptive learning requires the integration of validated learner models, pedagogically grounded adaptation rules, interoperable learning platforms and a teacher-in-the-loop approach. A set of requirements for national adaptive learning systems is proposed.

title: A Qualitative Study on Food Waste Management in Food and Beverage Businesses: The Case of Beykoz District
summary: Sustainability and food waste management have become central to the global agenda in response to the rapid depletion of natural resources and escalating environmental challenges. The food and beverage sector, in particular, constitutes a critical component of these discussions due to its intensive consumption of energy and water, as well as the substantial amounts of waste generated throughout production and consumption processes. The aim of this study is to conduct an in-depth qualitative analysis of food waste management practices within food and beverage establishments, alongside an examination of their potential for digital transformation. In this context, the study explores businesses’ levels of awareness regarding waste management, their digital infrastructures, their engagement with smart technologies such as the Internet of Things (IoT), and their perceptions of sustainability. The research population comprises restaurants and cafés operating in the Beykoz district of Istanbul Data were collected through semi-structured, face-to-face interviews conducted with the managers or owners of eight establishments selected via purposive sampling. The data obtained were analyzed using qualitative content analysis. The principal findings indicate that waste management practices within these establishments are generally confined to compliance with legal requirements and the implementation of ad hoc practical measures. Systematic approaches such as source separation of waste and technology-supported inventory management remain limited. Furthermore, the findings reveal a low level of awareness concerning digitalisation and IoT technologies, while cost pressures and operational intensity emerge as significant barriers to the adoption of sustainable practices. These results suggest that local authorities should develop incentive-based policies, organise targeted training programmes, and provide support for digital infrastructure in order to facilitate the transition towards sustainable and smart restaurant models within the sector.

title: Construction supply chain performance in mechanical and electrical contracts
summary: Purpose The fragmented nature of the construction industry makes supply chain management even more challenging. Even though Mechanical and Engineering work can represent a significant part of a typical construction project and have a significant impact on the overall project's success, strategies for managing these unique supply chains remain under-researched. This research explored how generic construction supply chain management strategies could be used to leverage the performance of the Mechanical and Engineering supply chains. Design/methodology/approach A questionnaire survey was conducted to obtain the views of construction professionals on the importance of seven key construction supply chain management strategies for the Mechanical and Engineering supply chain performance and the extent to which those strategies are visible within Mechanical and Engineering projects. Findings Selection Strategy, Communication, Site Coordination, Trust and Partnering agreements are the key generic strategies currently driving the performance of the M&E supply chain projects. Risk allocation and early design involvement strategies could be used to further improve M&E supply chain performance. Practical implications The results identified several factors considered critical to M&E supply chain performance but not currently being utilised to their full potential. This highlights opportunities for practitioners to implement targeted strategies to address these gaps in practice, thereby enhancing the overall performance of M&E supply chains. Originality/value This research contributed to the knowledge by investigating how to improve supply chain performance for an under-researched and important segment of the construction industry.

title: Artificial intelligence as academic infrastructure: governance, administrative intelligence, and AI fluency in Kazakhstan’s higher education sector
summary: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is increasingly part of higher education's institutional infrastructure, extending beyond teaching and learning to governance, administration, and student support. This study examines how AI Governance Readiness (AIGR) influences Administrative Efficiency through AI (AEAI), AI Fluency Orientation (AIFO), and Student Retention Intentions (SRI), while assessing the mediating roles of AEAI and AIFO and the moderating role of Equity Perception (EPS) in Kazakhstan's higher education sector. Drawing on Dynamic Capability Theory and Sociotechnical Systems Theory, the study develops and empirically tests an institutional capability model using 935 valid responses from students, faculty, academic administrators, and digital administration staff across public and private universities. The scholars analyzed the data using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) in SmartPLS 4.0, supported by RStudio. The measurement model demonstrated satisfactory reliability, convergent validity, and discriminant validity, while the structural model showed adequate explanatory and predictive performance. We assessed common method bias through procedural safeguards and full-collinearity diagnostics, and identified no substantive concerns. The findings show that AIGR is positively associated with AEAI and AIFO, while both constructs positively influence SRI. AEAI and AIFO also significantly mediate the relationship between AIGR and SRI. However, EPS does not significantly moderate the relationships between AI-enabled institutional capabilities and retention intentions. The findings position AI governance as a strategic institutional capability through which universities can improve administrative responsiveness, develop AI-related competencies, and support student continuity. The study contributes empirical evidence from Kazakhstan to the growing literature on responsible AI governance and digital transformation in higher education.

title: Digital strategy, ESG integration, and green supply chain efficiency in the Thai Agri-food industry: evidence from an undesirable-output SBM-DEA and system GMM analysis
summary: Agri-food processing drives Thailand's exports but is also a significant source of greenhouse gas emissions. This study examines whether digital strategy and environmental, social and governance (ESG) integration raise objectively measured green supply chain efficiency, and whether the two levers are complementary. A non-oriented, variable returns to scale modified slacks-based measure with Scope 1 and 2 emissions as an undesirable output is estimated for listed agri-food firms over 2021 to 2025; because emission disclosure is incomplete, efficiency is obtained for 172 firm-years of 42 firms from a frame of 51 firms. The score, interpreted as focal-firm supply chain eco-efficiency, is modeled with two-step system GMM on 86 firm-years of 33 firms, complemented by pooled, bias-corrected fixed effects, fractional probit, and selection-corrected estimates. Mean efficiency is 0.548. In the system GMM, digital intensity is negatively associated with efficiency (β = −0.677, p = 0.005), while ESG integration and the digital-ESG interaction are not significant. The interaction is nevertheless positive in almost every specification and significant in pooled (β = 0.184, p < 0.001), bias-corrected fixed effects ( p < 0.001), and fractional probit ( p = 0.037) estimates, and the marginal effect of digital intensity turns positive only at the highest ESG ratings. Productivity growth stems from catching up rather than frontier advance. The evidence is consistent with complementarity, in which digital investment improves eco-efficiency only when directed by strong sustainability integration, although the short panel limits the precision of the dynamic estimates. The study provides replicable frontier evidence from an emerging-market industry.

title: Determinants of AI Scribe Adoption in Allied Health: Mixed Methods Study Guided by the Capability, Opportunity, and Motivation Model for Behavior Change
summary: Background: AI scribes are emerging tools designed to reduce clinician documentation burden and improve clinical quality and efficiency by transcribing and documenting patient interactions in real-time. Despite growing evidence of their efficacy and impact across medical disciplines, there remains limited research on factors that influence successful implementation, particularly in allied health practice. Objective: This study explored the factors influencing the adoption of an AI scribe, including barriers and enablers among allied health clinicians, to inform ongoing implementation in public health settings. Methods: A mixed methods design was employed within a large Australian hospital and health service. Data were collected through surveys (n=97) and semistructured interviews (n=27) with allied health clinicians across multiple disciplines, including both adopters and nonadopters of an AI scribe. Survey data were analyzed descriptively. Interview transcripts were coded and thematically analyzed using a deductive approach guided by the COM-B (Capability, Opportunity, Motivation-Behavior) model to identify determinants of behavior. Results: Adoption was shaped by factors that could function as both barriers and enablers across the domains of capability, opportunity, and motivation. Enablers included tailored training, technology literacy, access to equipment and suitable recording spaces, leadership and peer support, and clear organizational communication. The absence of these factors, along with time and capacity constraints and unclear processes, hindered adoption. Responses to change, perceptions of the AI scribe's value, safety, reliability, and privacy, and prior experience with similar tools also influenced adoption, depending on individual perspectives. Conclusions: The successful implementation of an AI scribe in allied health settings requires multifaceted strategies that address COM-B factors. Key priorities include allocating sufficient time for uptake and adoption, providing tailored training, ensuring access to relevant resources, fostering leadership and peer support, and providing organizational direction. These findings offer actionable insights to guide future implementation efforts and advance digital transformation in allied health practice.

title: DOMAIN-SPECIFIC AND INCREMENTAL PREDICTIVE MODELING OF CREATIVITY AND HEALTH INFORMATION MANAGEMENT PRACTICE PERFORMANCE IN TERTIARY HOSPITALS IN SOUTH-SOUTH NIGERIA
summary: Background: Creativity has become increasingly relevant to health information management (HIM) practice as digital transformation demands professionals capable of adaptive problem-solving, data analysis, innovative thinking, and effective application of specialized competencies. This study examined the domain-specific and incremental predictive contribution of creativity to the performance of HIM practice in tertiary hospitals in South-South Nigeria. Methodology: This cross-sectional study included 124 HIM professionals from the University of Benin Teaching Hospital, University of Calabar Teaching Hospital, and University of Port Harcourt Teaching Hospital. The performance of HIM practice was assessed across four domains: electronic data entry, disease coding and indexing, clinical data analysis, and clinical research. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, simple linear regression, and hierarchical multiple regression. Results: Creativity demonstrated a strong positive correlation with overall HIM practice performance (r = 0.987, p < .001) and all individual practice domains (r = 0.964, t 0.981, p < .001). Domain-specific regression showed that creativity significantly predicted electronic data entry (R^2 = .939), disease coding and indexing (R^2 = .930), clinical data analysis (R^2 = .961), and clinical research practice (R^2 = .962). Creativity explained 97.5% of the variance in the overall performance of HIM practice. After controlling for age and hospital, its inclusion contributed an additional 53.1% of explained variance (R^2 = .531, p < .001). Conclusion: Creativity has a substantial positive predictive association with HIM practice performance across operational, analytical, and research functions. To strengthen HIM practice performance, tertiary hospitals should institutionalize creativity-oriented professional development incorporating innovative problem-solving, digital competencies, clinical coding, data analytics, and research skills to strengthen HIM practice performance.

title: Impact of festival season on supply chain disruptions in Bangladesh: challenges and strategies
summary: Purpose Festival seasons in Bangladesh generate predictable yet severe supply chain disruptions driven by demand surges, labour shortages and logistics congestion. While disruption research predominantly focuses on unexpected crises, recurrent culturally embedded disruptions remain underexplored. This study investigates how festival season pressures affect supply chain performance, modelling disruptions as a mediating mechanism and mitigation strategies as moderating capabilities. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative, cross-sectional survey collected data from 384 supply chain professionals across apparel, fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG), retail, logistics, and e-commerce sectors in Bangladesh. Construct validity was established through composite reliability (CR) and average variance extracted (AVE); discriminant validity via Fornell–Larcker and Heterotrait-monotrait (HTMT) criteria. Regression-based mediation and moderation analyses were conducted using PROCESS macro with 5,000 bootstrap samples. Findings Festival-season pressures are significantly associated with increased supply chain disruptions, which in turn negatively relate to performance. Consistent with full mediation, disruptions account for the pressure performance relationship. Mitigation strategies, demand forecasting, inventory buffering, supplier diversification and workforce planning are significantly associated with an attenuation of both the disruptive effect of festival pressures and disruptions’ negative relationship with performance. Practical implications Managers should adopt anticipatory, data-driven approaches including proactive inventory positioning and digital logistics integration. Policymakers should invest in infrastructure resilience and institutional capacity building. Originality/value This study advances institutional, resource dependence and dynamic capability theories by demonstrating that predictable, culturally embedded disruptions require anticipatory management capabilities in emerging economy contexts.

title: Sustainable finance taxonomies from a human rights perspective
summary: This article examines the human rights compatibility of 15 sustainable finance taxonomies issued by private transnational and international institutions as of June 2025. Addressing a gap in the literature, it derives the human rights responsibilities of taxonomy issuers based on the UN Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights and the OECD Due Diligence Guidance, viewing these issuers as business entities and collaborative governance initiatives (CGI). We argue that these standards impose responsibilities on taxonomy issuers, both in the governance of their frameworks and in the expectations they set for taxonomy users. While most taxonomies make some reference to human rights, few incorporate meaningful participatory standards in their governance structures, and only one includes substantive human rights requirements for users. None of the taxonomies provide adequate grievance mechanisms to challenge, for example, how a methodology is defined or applied to specific economic activities. Given the significant leverage of taxonomy issuers, we conclude that they need to incorporate human rights due diligence, robust assurance processes, participatory governance and grievance mechanisms, as well as access to remedy regarding the design of the taxonomies and the application of taxonomies by member institutions.

title: Supply-chain-aware input–output tables: reintroducing wholesale and retail flows
summary: The COVID-19 pandemic and the Suez Canal blockage have shown how disruptions to wholesalers, retailers, and logistics intermediaries can ripple across entire economies. Yet the input–output (IO) tables commonly used to study such cascading effects abstract these intermediaries away: they record only the margins charged by traders, not the products flowing through them. We develop a method to reintroduce these wholesale and retail flows into national IO tables, using Eurostat data calibrated against Austrian trade statistics. The resulting supply-chain IO (SC-IO) tables cover 22 European countries over 2011–2020, preserve national accounting identities, and align more closely with firm-level business statistics than standard IO tables. Applied to a hypothetical disruption of food wholesaling in Austria, they yield economic loss estimates several times larger than standard IO tables. The SC-IO tables provide a building block for resilience analysis, agent-based modeling, and policy assessment of trade and logistics disruptions.
